column1: # Case table for check-git-guard, read by BOTH runners' test suites
# (tests/test-git-guard.sh and tests/test-git-guard.ps1). One table means the
# two suites cannot drift, which is the failure mode this file exists to
# prevent: the .ps1 once had a bug the .sh did not, and no test caught it.
# Tab-separated, four or five columns:
#   expect  exit code the hook must return (0 = allowed, 2 = blocked)
#   mode    json   = wrap the command in a PreToolUse payload
#           bare   = feed the command as raw stdin (the no-jq fallback path)
#           parsed = like json, but the verdict only holds when the command is
#                    really extracted from the payload. The .ps1 always parses
#                    JSON; the .sh only when jq is installed, and scanning the
#                    raw payload cannot tell a '\n' escape from a space. The
#                    Bash suite skips these when jq is absent.
#   command the command text; \n means a line break
#   label   what the case is called in the output
#   title   optional: substring the block message must contain, so a case
#           cannot pass by tripping the wrong rule
# Lines starting with # are comments; #> starts a new section heading.
#> staging named paths and committing is allowed
#> bulk staging is blocked
#> plain pushing is allowed
